QUOTE: Form: `tool` or `tool:argpattern`. Both halves are `fnmatch` globs with no `FNM_PATHNAME`... Tool-only (no colon): matches the tool name alone, so it covers every call to that tool. With a colon: the tool part must match the tool name. The full pattern must then match `tool:<arg>`
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states fnmatch globbing, the tool/argument split on a colon, and that a colon-less pattern matches the tool name alone. It never says "split at the first colon" in those words, but the tool-part/arg-part split is clear.
